===== ORIGINAL PROMPT (initial_prompt.md) =====
Build a polished, fully offline-first iOS voice-journaling app called
"Fieldnotes". Native Apple stack only: SwiftUI + SwiftData, AVFoundation
for recording, Speech framework for on-device transcription, Natural­
Language framework for on-device tagging/sentiment, PencilKit for sketch
annotations. No backend, no accounts, no network dependency for any core
feature — everything must work in airplane mode. Follow the
ios-app-factory-rules. If a requested capability needs something this
project genuinely cannot provide (a special Apple entitlement, a paid
developer account feature, server-side ML), do NOT fake or stub it —
record it as an explicit gap with what it would actually take.

Core features (complete over broad — ship fewer things fully working):

1. Voice entries: record audio journal entries with a live waveform
   view while recording. Recording must survive being interrupted by a
   phone call, Siri, or the app being backgrounded, and must resume
   or cleanly finalize the entry rather than corrupt/lose it — get
   AVAudioSession category/interruption handling genuinely right, this
   is the hardest technical part of the app.
2. On-device transcription: transcribe each recording using Speech
   framework (on-device recognition only — reject/flag if only
   server-based recognition is available for a locale). Transcript is
   editable after the fact; edits must not desync from the audio
   timeline (tapping a transcript sentence seeks the audio to that
   point).
3. Auto-tagging & mood: run NaturalLanguage tokenization/sentiment on
   each transcript to suggest tags and a mood score. Suggestions are
   editable/dismissible — never silently apply an AI guess as fact.
4. Sketch annotations: attach PencilKit sketches to any entry (finger
   or Pencil), stored alongside the audio/transcript.
5. Bi-directional linking: entries can @-mention/link other entries;
   each entry shows a "linked from" backlinks section computed live
   from the local store (no manual backlink maintenance) — same
   integrity discipline as a graph/notes app: linking, unlinking, and
   deleting an entry must never leave a dangling or duplicate backlink.
6. Search: full-text search across transcripts AND tags/mood, with
   results ranked by a real relevance score you define and document
   (not just substring match order).
7. HealthKit correlation (read-only, explicit permission): show each
   entry's mood alongside that day's HealthKit sleep/activity summary
   if authorized, and degrade to "not connected" honestly if denied —
   never block core journaling on this permission.
8. Home-screen widget + Live Activity: widget shows the latest entry's
   mood/snippet; a Live Activity shows elapsed time and live waveform
   while actively recording, ending cleanly when the recording stops
   or the app is killed mid-recording (no orphaned Live Activity).
9. Share Extension (separate target): accept shared text or a photo
   from other apps and create a new Fieldnotes entry from it.
10. App Intents: "Start a voice entry" and "Search my journal" exposed
    to Shortcuts/Siri.
11. CarPlay: a minimal CarPlay scene for hands-free start/stop
    recording while driving. This requires Apple's CarPlay audio-app
    entitlement, which a personal free developer account cannot
    obtain — if that's confirmed true in this environment, build the
    CarPlay scene code path correctly but record in Gaps that it
    cannot actually run/ship without that entitlement, rather than
    silently omitting the feature or pretending it works.

Priorities, in order: (a) audio-session interruption correctness — a
lost or corrupted recording is the worst possible failure, (b) backlink
graph integrity, (c) honest degradation of every permission-gated
feature (Speech, HealthKit, CarPlay). Use Decimal/Int for anything
numeric that isn't inherently floating (durations in seconds as
TimeInterval is fine; don't invent unnecessary Decimal use here — this
app's money-precision lesson from prior apps doesn't apply, there's no
currency). Seed a "demo entries" toggle in Settings with realistic
sample entries, transcripts, tags, and backlinks so no screen is empty
on first review. Provide a clear way to run it in the iOS Simulator via
Xcode, and call out anywhere CarPlay/HealthKit/Speech behave differently
in Simulator vs. a real device.

CONSENSUS: YES

Fieldnotes is one app, not a portfolio. The prompt named a single product with one cohesive value proposition — voice + timeline-anchored transcript + tags/mood + live backlinks + HealthKit context, all sharing one offline local graph. The widget, Live Activity, Share Extension, App Intents, and CarPlay scene are all surfaces of that same product (and, per the App Group + shared SwiftData container decision from earlier phases, they *must* read/write the same local store) — splitting them into sibling projects would break the exact integrity guarantees the earlier phases spent two rounds locking down. There's no requested category being collapsed here; there was only ever one category requested, so no portfolio-json manifest is needed.

Selected app: **Fieldnotes** (slug: `fieldnotes`, category: journaling / personal-knowledge / wellness, build: true) — an offline-first, privacy-preserving iOS voice journal for a privacy-first solo journaler who needs reliable capture through real-life interruptions and wants a searchable, linked, offline archive they can trust completely.

Widget/Live Activity are secondary, Share Extension/App Intents tertiary, CarPlay is a compiling code path with an honest gap note and zero polish time.   constraints: Build verification must still independently produce the real named-scenario, multi-run evidence; this phase's criterion cannot be cited as substitute
- [DEC-app_features-006] Information architecture for this phase is confirmed as three tabs (Timeline, Search, Record entry point, Entry Detail as pushed screen), matching Codex's screen-by-screen flow mapping and reaffirming DEC-initial_discussion-004 with no changes.
  rationale: Codex's IA/UX pass (Timeline -> Record -> Entry Detail -> Search flows, with explicit interruption/transcription state visibility at each screen) is fully consistent with the already-locked three-tab structure, so it's adopted as this phase's screen-level elaboration rather than a new IA decision.
  rejected: Introducing new screens or a different tab structure at this phase
  constraints: Build must implement exactly the screens and states named in this round's IA pass (Timeline entry preview with mood chip, Record screen with interruption-state UI, Entry Detail with tap-to-seek + backlinks, Search with ranked results)
- [DEC-design_discussion-001] Design language is 'Analog Field Journal' — paper field-notebook visuals crossed with an analog tape recorder's honest VU-meter feedback language, chosen over Codex's more generic 'Journal of Thoughts' framing.
  rationale: Both participants converged on a paper/journal metaphor with warm, muted tones, but Claude's pass gave it a specific, non-swappable identity (ink-waveform, visible interruption seam, instrument-panel dark mode) that satisfies the phase's acceptance check that the language be specific to this app; Codex's naming was generic enough to fit most journaling apps and added no conflicting content.
  rejected: Codex's 'Journal of Thoughts' as the canonical name; A generic 'clean and modern' design language
  constraints: All later design/build phases must reference 'Analog Field Journal' as the app's design language and apply its ink-waveform/paper-palette/instrument-panel vocabulary consistently
- [DEC-design_discussion-002] Emotional target is quiet reliability ('this caught what I said, even through the mess of real life'), not delight or gamified positivity.
  rationale: The product's core promise (DEC-initial_discussion-001) is trust under interruption, not engagement; the emotional target must reflect that rather than default app-store cheerfulness.
  rejected: A delight/gamified emotional target
  constraints: UI copy and motion design in later phases must be judged against calm reliability, not excitement or reward framing
- [DEC-design_discussion-003] Signature interaction is the ink-style live waveform that visibly changes color/state at the exact moment of interruption and resumes in a distinguishable shade, rather than hiding the interruption behind a spinner or generic 'resuming...' toast.
  rationale: This is the one screen moment that can concretely earn user trust in the app's hardest technical guarantee (interruption safety); hiding it behind a spinner would throw away the app's best chance to demonstrate the thing it's proudest of.
  rejected: A generic spinner or 'resuming...' toast during interruption recovery
  constraints: Build phase must implement the Record screen's interruption visual as a distinct ink-color/glyph change at the point of interruption, not a generic loading indicator
- [DEC-design_discussion-004] The default stock-iOS look (plain List rows, system blue, nav-bar '+' record button, default push transitions) is explicitly rejected in favor of: card rows with a waveform ghost sparkline + mood chip + visible transcription-state badge; a warm paper/sepia (light) and charcoal instrument-panel (dark) palette reserving color for mood; and a tactile bottom-center circular record control reachable one-thumb from Timeline.
  rationale: A plain List/system-blue/nav-bar-icon app would look like a Voice Memos clone with tags bolted on and would bury exactly the state information (transcription status, mood) this app is contractually required to keep honest and visible; the target user capturing a 30s burst mid-interruption also needs a large, unmistakable record affordance, not a small icon.
  rejected: Plain List rows with title/subtitle text; System blue accent color; Nav-bar icon as the record entry point
  constraints: Build must implement custom card rows, the named palette, and the bottom-center record control per the theme file rule (Theme.swift), not default List/Form chrome
- [DEC-design_discussion-005] Screen inventory and per-screen state models are locked as: Timeline (empty/loading/populated/error + per-card transcribing/downloading/unavailable/ready badges + demo/real corner-ribbon marker), full-screen Record (idle/arming/recording/interrupted/finalizing/error), Entry Detail (loading/ready/unavailable-with-reason/editing + calm empty-backlinks state + distinct broken-link chip styling), Search (empty-query/no-matches-vs-nothing-indexed/ranked-results with a visible match-reason hint), and Settings (full mic/Speech/HealthKit permission matrix + prominent demo toggle + labeled Pro/CloudKit-gap entries).
  rationale: Elaborates the three-tab IA already locked in DEC-initial_discussion-004 and DEC-app_features-006 into concrete, buildable screen/state detail per this phase's playbook requirement, without introducing new screens or changing the tab structure.
  rejected: Leaving state models abstract/qualitative rather than enumerated per screen; Introducing additional screens beyond the locked three-tab + Entry Detail + Record structure
  constraints: Build phase must implement every named state (not a simplified subset) for each screen, since the global rule requires empty/loading/success/error states wherever a workflow can reach them
- [DEC-design_discussion-006] Demo vs. real entries are visually distinguished by a small corner-ribbon marker on Timeline cards, kept deliberately separate from mood color so the two signals never get confused.
  rationale: DEC-prompt_contract-009 and [REDACTED:high_entropy] require demo data to never be mistaken for real data; using mood's own color channel for that distinction would create exactly the ambiguity those decisions forbid.
  rejected: Using a distinct background color or tint to mark demo entries (risks colliding with mood color signal)
  constraints: Build must implement the demo/real marker as a separate visual element (ribbon/badge) from the mood color chip
- [DEC-design_discussion-007] Search results surface a visible, honest 'why this matched' hint (e.g. which of transcript/tag/mood matched) rather than presenting a mystery ranked order.
  rationale: The app already commits to a documented, non-substring relevance formula (DEC-prompt_contract-007, DEC-app_features-003); showing the match reason in the UI extends that same honesty principle to the visual layer instead of leaving ranking logic invisible to the user.
  rejected: Showing only a ranked list with no visible explanation of why an entry matched
  constraints: Search results UI must expose a lightweight match-reason indicator per result, computed from the same relevance formula used for ordering
- [DEC-design_discussion-008] Accessibility commitments for this design language: every color-coded element (mood chip, state badge) pairs with a text/VoiceOver label, the interruption ink-color change fires a simultaneous VoiceOver announcement, and at maximum Dynamic Type the waveform sparkline is dropped before it's allowed to collide with badges/chips.
  rationale: The ink-waveform and mood-color visual language is the biggest accessibility risk this phase introduces since so much of its meaning is color/motion-coded; explicit rules prevent the design language from silently excluding VoiceOver or low-vision users, and satisfy the global no-overlap rule under Dynamic Type stress.
  rejected: Relying on color alone for mood/state signaling; Allowing the sparkline to clip or overlap badges at large text sizes
  constraints: Build must implement text/VoiceOver labels alongside every color-coded UI element and a VoiceOver announcement at the interruption moment; Card layout must drop the sparkline before violating the no-overlap rule at largest Dynamic Type sizes
- [DEC-design_handoff-001] Navigation is a single TabView (Timeline/Search/Settings) each with its own NavigationStack; Record presents as a fullScreenCover (never a sheet or push); Entry Detail is pushed; @-mention autocomplete is an inline popover anchored to the transcript caret, not a sheet.
  rationale: Per-tab NavigationStacks prevent cross-tab scroll/detail-position bugs from a naively shared stack; Record's five distinct states (idle/arming/recording/interrupted/finalizing/error) need full-screen unambiguous modality per DEC-design_discussion-005 rather than competing for attention with content behind a sheet.
  rejected: Single shared NavigationStack across all tabs; Record as a sheet or pushed screen
  constraints: Build must implement Record as fullScreenCover specifically; a later refactor to push nav is disallowed since it would reopen a race between transcript editing and the interruption state machine
- [DEC-design_handoff-002] Transcription status, tag/mood suggestions, and backlinks must be read live off the SwiftData model on every render (via @Query / per-screen #Predicate) — never cached or snapshotted into view-model state.
  rationale: DEC-prompt_contract-008 requires backlinks to be a live query with zero stored bookkeeping and DEC-initial_discussion-003 requires the Timeline badge to update in place without blocking a new recording; a cached view-model snapshot would recreate the exact 'app lies about its own state' failure the product is designed to prevent.
  rejected: Caching transcription/backlink state in a @Published view-model field derived once; A global backlink index rebuilt on every entry save
  constraints: Timeline's @Query reads Entry directly from the shared App Group ModelContainer; Backlinks resolve via a per-screen #Predicate query computed at Entry Detail render time, not a precomputed global index
- [DEC-design_handoff-003] Transcription runs as one background Task per entry, not a shared serializing queue actor.
  rationale: A shared queue actor would serialize entries behind each other, violating DEC-initial_discussion-003's requirement that a second recording is never blocked by a prior entry's in-progress transcription.
  rejected: A single shared actor-based transcription queue
  constraints: Build must implement per-entry background Tasks that write status updates onto the Entry model on the main actor
- [DEC-design_handoff-004] The live waveform (WaveformInkView) consumes a throttled, downsampled amplitude stream (~12-15 updates/sec, RMS per bucket) from the recording controller, never raw AVAudioEngine tap buffers.
  rationale: Drawing every raw sample as an ink stroke would pin the main thread and risk competing with the audio render thread for CPU — a dropped audio buffer during a demanding animation frame is the worst-case failure this app exists to prevent.
  rejected: Rendering directly from raw AVAudioEngine tap sample buffers
  constraints: Build must implement a throttled/downsampled amplitude publisher between the recording controller and WaveformInkView
- [DEC-design_handoff-005] Full design tokens are locked with explicit values: 7-step Dynamic-Type-mapped type scale, 4pt-base spacing grid (steps 4/8/12/16/24/32/48), 4-step corner radii (8/14/20/999), and a 9-role semantic color palette with both light and dark hex values for every role.
  rationale: Satisfies the phase's hard acceptance check that a SwiftUI builder can write Theme.swift with zero invented values; no adjective stands in for a number anywhere in the spec.
  rejected: Leaving any token as a qualitative description for the build phase to interpret
  constraints: Build must implement Theme.swift from these exact values and reference it everywhere; no scattered font/size/color literals in views
- [DEC-design_handoff-006] Text-secondary color #A79C89 on dark surface #26231F is flagged as a borderline contrast case requiring an actual computed WCAG check before Theme.swift is finalized, rather than assumed compliant.
  rationale: Catching a potential accessibility failure at spec time is far cheaper than discovering it at QA or App Review; the design discussion phase already committed to explicit contrast expectations for this palette.
  rejected: Shipping the hex pair without a contrast verification step
  constraints: Build or verification phase must run a computed contrast check on this specific pair before sign-off
- [DEC-design_handoff-007] A full component inventory (EntryCard, WaveformInkView, RecordButton, InterruptionBanner, TranscriptAnchorText, TagChip/MoodChip, BacklinkRow, SketchThumbnail, SearchResultRow, PermissionMatrixRow, DemoRibbon) is locked, each mapped to its screen(s), including specific empty/error copy per screen and specific motion/haptic timings (300ms interruption crossfade, 200ms badge crossfade, distinct haptics for arm/start/interruption/finalize).
  rationale: Directly satisfies the phase's required output for named components, per-screen states with real copy (not TBD), and motion/haptics notes, closing off any hidden decisions the build phase would otherwise have to invent.
  rejected: Leaving component boundaries or state copy for the build phase to decide
  constraints: Build must implement RecordButton as one component with continuous state transitions, not five conditional views; Search's two empty states (nothing indexed vs. no matches) must use visibly distinct copy
- [DEC-design_handoff-008] No external Claude Design pass is used for this app; the build phase implements Theme.swift and the component set directly from this handoff's spec. An optional fallback prompt for the Record screen alone is provided in case a second opinion is wanted, but it is not required for handoff completion.
  rationale: The visual system is already fully specified (named palette with hex values, named components, per-screen state models, a timed signature interaction); an external design pass risks reinventing generic 'clean and modern' and discarding the ink-waveform/paper-palette identity established over two prior phases.
  rejected: Routing the Record screen or full app through an external Claude Design pass
  constraints: If the coordinator later chooses to run the fallback prompt, its output must be reconciled against this spec's Record-screen state model and signature-interaction rules, not treated as a replacement for them
- [[REDACTED:high_entropy]] The main app target enables Background Modes → Audio, and AVAudioSession uses category .playAndRecord with .allowBluetooth and .defaultToSpeaker, activated only while Record is presented or audio is playing and deactivated otherwise.
  rationale: Without the audio background mode, iOS suspends the process within seconds of backgrounding and AVAudioEngine's render thread stops — making requirement #1 (survive backgrounding) structurally impossible; this was never explicitly named in any earlier phase despite being the precondition for the entire interruption-safety story.
  rejected: Leaving background audio capability unstated and assuming it 'just works'; Holding the audio session active permanently rather than scoping it to Record/playback
  constraints: Build must declare Background Modes → Audio in Info.plist; Audio session activation/deactivation must be scoped to Record presentation and Entry Detail playback, not held open permanently
- [[REDACTED:high_entropy]] Recording buffers are written incrementally to an on-disk AVAudioFile as they arrive from the AVAudioEngine tap, never held only in memory; on next launch the app scans for entries left in recording/interrupted status with no clean finalize and reconciles them from whatever was actually flushed to disk, marking a truncated result 'recovered after unexpected exit.'
  rationale: An in-memory buffer dies with the process on force-quit — one of the five named interruption scenarios — which would cause exactly the worst-case failure (silent data loss) this entire project exists to prevent.
  rejected: Buffering the full take in memory and writing it out only on stop
  constraints: Build must implement incremental disk writes per tap buffer; Build must implement a launch-time reconciliation scan with an honest 'recovered' state, never a silently corrupted or unopenable file
- [[REDACTED:high_entropy]] Every SwiftData @Model in the app is written CloudKit-compatible from the first commit (no @Attribute(.unique), all relationships optional with an inverse, every non-optional attribute has a default value), even though the CloudKit sync toggle ships off by default.
  rationale: CloudKit-backed SwiftData has real, unforgiving schema constraints; if the schema isn't written to satisfy them from day one, [REDACTED:high_entropy]'s 'config flip, not a migration' claim silently becomes false the moment someone tries to enable it later.
  rejected: Writing the initial schema without CloudKit constraints in mind and treating compatibility as a future migration task
  constraints: Build must validate every model against CloudKit's SwiftData constraints even with the toggle off
- [[REDACTED:high_entropy]] The shared data model layer (Entry, Anchor, Tag, Mood, Sketch, Mention) lives in one local Swift Package imported identically by the main app, widget extension, Share Extension, and CarPlay code path; audio files are stored as real files in the App Group container via FileManager (SwiftData stores only the relative path), and PencilKit drawings are stored as @Attribute(.externalStorage) Data.
  rationale: A copy-pasted @Model definition per target risks schema drift the first time someone edits one target and forgets the others — a subtler bug than a missing feature since it only surfaces on a specific cross-target read/write path; storing large audio artifacts as real files rather than SQLite blobs means a corrupted store file doesn't risk the entire recording archive.
  rejected: Duplicating @Model definitions per target; Storing audio as SwiftData-managed blobs inside the SQLite store
  constraints: Build must create one local Swift Package for the shared schema, imported by every target that touches the App Group store; Audio persists as files in the App Group container with only a relative path in SwiftData
- [[REDACTED:high_entropy]] The interruption state machine exposes directly callable methods (handleInterruption(type:options:), handleRouteChange(reason:)) with NotificationCenter reduced to a thin forwarding adapter, enabling pure-logic XCTest coverage in CI; the five named real-world interruption scenarios remain a separate manual physical-device test tier that CI cannot substitute for.
  rationale: If the state machine is only reachable via live AVAudioSession notifications it is untestable in CI, since Simulator cannot generate a real incoming call or Bluetooth route change; splitting into two explicit tiers prevents either tier from being mistaken for satisfying the other.
  rejected: Wiring interruption handling directly inside the NotificationCenter observer closures with no separately callable/testable entry points
  constraints: Build must expose state-machine transition methods independently of NotificationCenter for CI unit testing; tech_specs/build-verification must record CI unit-test coverage and the manual real-device scenario pass as two distinct deliverables, not one blurred testing line
- [[REDACTED:high_entropy]] Permissions are locked concretely: separate honest-copy NSMicrophoneUsageDescription and NSSpeechRecognitionUsageDescription strings; HealthKit requests NSHealthShareUsageDescription only (no write permission) and reads exactly HKCategoryType(.sleepAnalysis) plus HKQuantityType(.stepCount) or .activeEnergyBurned; a .storekit configuration file is checked into the repo so the airplane-mode-after-purchase test case is runnable in Simulator without a sandbox account.
  rationale: Generic boilerplate permission copy is an App Review flag, and 'HealthKit correlation' as a phrase isn't an implementable spec until the exact read types are named; a checked-in .storekit file is what makes [REDACTED:high_entropy]'s test case actually runnable.
  rejected: Leaving HealthKit read types unspecified until build time; Relying on a live sandbox Apple ID for StoreKit testing instead of a local .storekit config
  constraints: Info.plist must include both mic and speech usage strings with real explanatory copy; HealthKit read set is limited to sleep analysis and one activity metric (steps or active energy), read-only; A .storekit config file must exist in the repo for local subscription testing
- [[REDACTED:high_entropy]] Dependency policy is finalized as zero third-party packages; full-text search is implemented as a plain in-memory scored pass over @Query-fetched entries rather than adopting GRDB/FTS5 or any other search library.
  rationale: At the realistic data scale of a personal voice journal (hundreds to low thousands of entries), a first-party in-memory scoring pass is correct and sufficient, and it keeps the tech-stack's permissive-dependency policy trivially satisfied by simply not needing an exception.
  rejected: Adopting GRDB/SQLite FTS5 or another third-party search library for relevance ranking
  constraints: tech_specs must implement search as an in-memory scoring function over SwiftData query results, not a new persistence/search dependency
- [DEC-tech_specs-001] Architecture is MVVM-lite where views bind directly to @Query/@Model and the only real service layer is either a stateful machine owning one hard problem (RecordingController) or a pure function reading the store (SearchRelevanceScorer, BacklinkQuery, MentionAutocompleteQuery) — no general-purpose view models holding derived state.
  rationale: design_handoff already mandated live SwiftData reads over cached view-model state; this phase extends that principle into the full architecture so no builder has a natural place to reintroduce a stale snapshot.
  rejected: Traditional MVVM with @Published view-model properties mirroring model state
  constraints: Any new service added during build must be classified as either a stateful actor or a pure function over the store, not a cached intermediary
- [DEC-tech_specs-002] Entry gains a mutable title field (short human-readable label) distinct from its immutable UUID identity, used for @-mention display/autocomplete UI.
  rationale: DEC-prompt_contract-014 requires mentions to resolve by UUID never title text, but a human still needs something readable to search/select in the autocomplete UI; without a title field there was no such string in the data model.
  rejected: Deriving a display label from the first N characters of the transcript at query time
  constraints: Autocomplete and backlink UI must display Entry.title, but all mention resolution/storage must still use UUID, never title text
- [DEC-tech_specs-003] Entry.cachedTranscriptText is a denormalized, single-writer cache (rebuilt only by a dedicated TranscriptEditor.applyEdit(anchorID:newText:) entry point) that concatenates non-deleted Anchor text, used so search doesn't fault in every entry's anchor relationship on every keystroke.
  rationale: Without a cache, search over a seeded 60+ entry demo set faults in every Anchor relationship per query, which is fine in a two-entry test case and janky at realistic demo scale; a single enforced write path keeps it from becoming a second, driftable source of truth.
  rejected: Querying Anchor relationships live on every search pass with no cache; Allowing any code path to write Anchor.text directly
  constraints: All transcript text edits must go through TranscriptEditor.applyEdit, never direct Anchor.text mutation, or the cache can desync from the anchors it's derived from
- [DEC-tech_specs-004] Entry.waveformSummary (~48 RMS buckets, computed once at finalize) persists the recording's amplitude shape for the Timeline's EntryCard ghost sparkline, rendered with a deterministic per-entry ink-color seed derived from mood plus a hash of the entry id.
  rationale: The component inventory from design_handoff needs persisted waveform data for EntryCard (not just the live recording view), and computing it once at finalize is free since the RMS buckets already exist from the live waveform pipeline; the per-entry color seed turns a generic sparkline into a distinguishing visual signature consistent with the 'Analog Field Journal' identity.
  rejected: Re-deriving a sparkline from the raw audio file on each Timeline render; Uniform gray sparkline styling for all entries
  constraints: waveformSummary must be computed and persisted exactly once, at finalize, not recomputed on every render
- [DEC-tech_specs-005] Mention.targetEntryID is stored as a raw UUID field, not a SwiftData relationship, and Anchor uses soft-delete (isDeleted flag, text cleared, id/position preserved) rather than hard row deletion.
  rationale: A SwiftData relationship for targetEntryID would either require a non-optional inverse SwiftData can't express or silently null out on delete, defeating broken-link detection; soft-deleting Anchor is what makes the nearest-surviving-anchor tap fallback ([REDACTED:high_entropy]) implementable, since the id and position must survive even when content doesn't.
  rejected: Modeling Mention.target as a SwiftData relationship with cascade/nullify on delete; Hard-deleting Anchor rows on transcript edit
  constraints: Broken-mention detection must check whether targetEntryID resolves to an existing Entry via context.model(for:), not rely on relationship nullification; Anchor deletion in the UI must map to isDeleted=true + text='', never an actual row removal
- [DEC-tech_specs-006] The search relevance formula is fixed with exact point weights: 3pts/query-token as a whole-word transcript match plus 5pts for the full phrase as a contiguous substring, 5pts per exact tag-name match, 4pts for a mood-label token match, and a recency bonus (2/1/0 pts on a 15-day step decay) that only applies on top of a nonzero content match, never standalone; entries scoring 0 total are excluded from results.
  rationale: Three prior phases (prompt_contract, app_features, design_discussion) promised a documented relevance formula without ever writing the actual weights down; this closes that gap with concrete numbers and a worked two-entry proof case (query 'beach calm': Entry A scores 8, Entry B scores 4).
  rejected: Leaving the formula as a qualitative 'weighted' description for build to interpret; Letting recency alone surface an entry with zero real content match
  constraints: SearchRelevanceScorer.score must be pure/deterministic and unit-tested against the fixed two-entry case with exact expected scores, not just relative ordering
- [DEC-tech_specs-007] Concurrency boundaries are: main actor owns ModelContext and UI; RecordingController is its own actor exposing handleInterruption/handleRouteChange as directly callable methods with NotificationCenter as a thin forwarding shim; TranscriptionCoordinator spawns one Task per entry (no shared queue actor); domain-specific typed errors (RecordingError, TranscriptionError, HealthKitError) always resolve to a visible UI state, with no try? anywhere in the recording or finalize path.
  rationale: Directly implements ios_architecture_review's CI-testability requirement (state machine must be callable without live AVAudioSession notifications) and design_handoff's per-entry-Task rule, while the no-try?-in-finalize rule enforces the product's core promise that the app never silently swallows a recording failure.
  rejected: Wiring interruption/route-change handling only inside NotificationCenter closures; Using try? or silent catches anywhere in the recording/finalize path
  constraints: Build must grep-verify no try? exists in RecordingController's recording/finalize code path as part of code review
- [DEC-tech_specs-008] Testing strategy is split into FieldnotesCoreTests (CI, zero hardware: state machine transitions including the reentrant double-interruption case, anchor fallback, mention dedup/self-mention rejection, the search formula asserted with exact scores, StoreKit entitlement logic against the checked-in .storekit file, and DemoDataSeeder idempotency/reversal) versus a separate physical-device manual tier (five named interruption scenarios, tap-to-seek ≤300ms tolerance surviving an edit, VoiceOver interruption-announcement spot-check, airplane-mode-immediately-after-purchase Pro check) that CI cannot substitute for.
  rationale: Directly operationalizes ios_architecture_review's two-tier testing split into a concrete, named test list rather than leaving it as an abstract policy, so build verification has an actual checklist to execute against.
  rejected: A single blended testing checklist that doesn't distinguish CI-provable claims from device-only claims
  constraints: Build verification must report these two tiers as separate deliverables, matching [REDACTED:high_entropy]
- [DEC-project_plan-001] Milestone 0 is a hard gate: scaffold all four targets (main app, widget extension, Share Extension, CarPlay) as empty shells importing FieldnotesCore, configure the App Group capability, and prove a real cross-target write/read round-trip — before any feature code is written.
  rationale: Every target must import the identical shared schema from day one per the architecture review's schema-drift warning; retrofitting this after targets have diverged with their own convenience @Model copies is expensive and exactly the failure mode that decision existed to prevent.
  rejected: Treating App Group/shared-package setup as a soft early goal alongside feature work rather than a blocking gate
  constraints: No feature-lane work starts until the cross-target round-trip is demonstrated
- [DEC-project_plan-002] Milestones are sequenced by genuine data dependency rather than MoSCoW tier: infra gate -> data model/persistence -> recording pipeline -> transcription/tagging -> search -> backlinks -> demo seeding -> Should-tier (sketches/HealthKit/widget+LiveActivity/Share Extension) -> Could-tier (App Intents/Pro/CloudKit toggle) -> CarPlay code path last.
  rationale: MoSCoW tiers describe priority, not buildability order; recording must exist before transcription can run, transcription/tagging before search has content, and a stable schema before demo data is seeded (to avoid reseeding when the model changes).
  rejected: Sequencing milestones directly off the Must/Should/Could/Won't tiering from app_features
  constraints: Demo data seeding must not start until the full data model is stable; Search milestone cannot start meaningfully until recording+transcription produce real transcript content
- [DEC-project_plan-003] The pure-function data-layer components (SearchRelevanceScorer, BacklinkQuery, AutoTagger, MentionAutocompleteQuery) run as a parallel track starting alongside the recording pipeline milestone, since they operate on fixture data and don't require a working recorder — but wiring them to real UI against the interfaces-json types is a separately named, separately verified integration task.
  rationale: These are pure functions over fixture Entry/string data and have no dependency on the recording pipeline being done, which is a real parallelization opportunity; but building them against ad-hoc fixtures risks a second, quieter integration point where real wiring silently doesn't match interfaces-json, so that merge must be explicit rather than assumed.
  rejected: Sequencing pure-function components strictly behind the recording pipeline; Treating parallel-track integration as an automatic non-event with no dedicated verification step
  constraints: Integration of parallel-track components into real UI must be a named task with its own verification, not folded silently into a later milestone
- [DEC-project_plan-004] Verification tasks are scheduled as specific, separately-evidenced milestones rather than one end-of-plan testing bucket: (a) the real-incoming-call interruption scenario requires a second device to ring the test phone, decided as logistics now; (b) the low-storage scenario is tested via a debug-only synthetic 'report insufficient free space' hook rather than actually filling device storage; (c) CloudKit-readiness verification is scoped as a structural/lint-style schema-constraint check only, not a live CloudKit sync test.
  rationale: Generic 'testing' as a trailing bucket is exactly where this app's own success criteria (five named scenarios, structural CloudKit compliance) would likely get shortchanged; naming the mechanism for each risky/expensive test now prevents someone from attempting the costly or risky version (e.g. actually filling a device's disk) by default later.
  rejected: Leaving interruption/low-storage/CloudKit verification as generic line items under one testing phase; Testing low-storage by literally filling a physical device's disk
  constraints: Low-storage testing must use a synthetic injection hook, not real disk-filling; CloudKit verification tasks must not require provisioning a live CloudKit container
- [DEC-project_plan-005] DemoDataSeeder batches all its writes and calls WidgetCenter.reloadTimelines() exactly once at the end of the full seed operation, not per-entry-save.
  rationale: The 'reload only on confirmed save' rule from detailed_discussion is correct for the live recording flow but, applied literally to a 40-60 entry bulk seed, would exhaust most of the widget's finite daily reload budget in a single operation — a bug better prevented at plan time than discovered as a mystery 'widget stopped updating' issue during device testing.
  rejected: Applying the per-save widget reload rule literally to bulk demo seeding
  constraints: DemoDataSeeder implementation must call reloadTimelines() once after all seed writes complete, not once per entry
- [DEC-project_plan-006] A small, early, standalone task fact-checks the CarPlay audio-app entitlement requirement against Apple's actual developer documentation, before the CarPlay milestone or final Gaps documentation.
  rationale: This claim has been flagged as 'needs independent fact-checking' for four consecutive phases without anyone actually doing it; the project plan is the right place to stop deferring it so the Gaps doc states a verified fact rather than a repeated assumption.
  rejected: Continuing to carry the unverified assumption forward into build/verification phases
  constraints: This fact-check task must complete before the Gaps documentation asserts the CarPlay entitlement limitation as fact
- [DEC-task_assignments-001] Project file/target layout is locked: Fieldnotes.xcodeproj at root, Fieldnotes/ (main app, including CarPlaySceneDelegate as an in-app scene configuration, not a 5th Xcode target), FieldnotesWidget/, FieldnotesShare/, FieldnotesCore/ local Swift package, Config/ (.storekit file), Docs/ (run guide + Gaps/feature-health-card).
  rationale: CarPlay support is wired via a scene configuration inside the main app target's Info.plist per Apple's actual mechanism, not a separate .appex; modeling it as a literal fifth product target (as project_plan's shorthand implied) would not compile.

Build capable iPhone apps with **zero third-party dependencies**. For each framework: when to reach for it, the entry-point type, and a compilable, idiomatic snippet or the gotcha that bites people. ## General rules

- **Prefer these over SPM packages.** RevenueCat, Firebase Analytics, Lottie, Alamofire, etc. all have first-party equivalents good enough for most apps. Fewer deps = smaller binary, faster builds, no supply-chain risk, no privacy-manifest surprises.
- **Every framework that touches user data needs an `Info.plist` usage-description string** (or an entitlement). Missing it is a runtime crash the moment the API is used — not a compile error. The specific keys are listed per section.

## StoreKit 2 — In-App Purchase & Subscriptions

**Use it when:** you sell anything — consumables, non-consumables, or auto-renewable subscriptions. Replaces callback-based StoreKit 1 entirely.

**Start from:** `Product` (fetch + purchase) and `Transaction` (entitlements + history). No server strictly required — signatures are verified on-device via `VerificationResult`.

### The three things you must do

1. **Load products by ID** (IDs come from App Store Connect):

```swift
import StoreKit

let productIDs = ["com.app.pro.monthly", "com.app.pro.yearly", "com.app.coins.100"]
let products = try await Product.products(for: productIDs)   // async throws
```

2. **Purchase, then verify and finish the transaction:**

```swift
func purchase(_ product: Product) async throws -> Transaction? {
    let result = try await product.purchase()
    switch result {
    case .success(let verification):
        let transaction = try checkVerified(verification)
        await transaction.finish()          // REQUIRED — unfinished txns replay forever
        return transaction
    case .userCancelled, .pending:
        return nil
    @unknown default:
        return nil
    }
}

func checkVerified<T>(_ result: VerificationResult<T>) throws -> T {
    switch result {
    case .unverified(_, let error): throw error   // signature failed — do NOT grant
    case .verified(let safe):       return safe
    }
}
```

3. **Listen for `Transaction.updates` from app launch** — the single most-missed requirement. It catches renewals, Ask-to-Buy approvals, refunds, and purchases made on other devices.

```swift
// Start this in your App init / a top-level task and keep it alive for the app's lifetime.
func observeTransactions() -> Task<Void, Never> {
    Task.detached {
        for await update in Transaction.updates {
            guard case .verified(let transaction) = update else { continue }
            await grantEntitlement(for: transaction)   // your unlock logic
            await transaction.finish()
        }
    }
}
```

Use `Transaction.currentEntitlements` (an async sequence). **iOS 18.4+ note:** the per-product `Transaction.currentEntitlement(for:)` is deprecated in favor of `Transaction.currentEntitlements(for:)`, because a user can hold multiple entitling transactions (e.g. own it *and* have Family Sharing access).

```swift

        guard case .verified(let transaction) = result else { continue }
```
